how: The starter proposes the logo, supplies its location, and reports a tiny version already begun.
Calls ask readers to collaborate on and help build the logo, while related logos provide context rather than documented outside recruits.
A reader explicitly joins the collaboration call without requesting anything in return.
A proposed expansion receives brief assent without a reciprocal request.
Anchor coordinates locate the attempt, while a reader asks for a neighbouring logo as an additional landmark.
The starter reports a tiny light blue logo already placed at the coordinates while seeking more help.
An edited comment reports completed letters while explaining the retained black border.
Participants propose extending the letters, choose a darker blue, approve ideas, and invite critique of another expansion.
Participants identify people applying competing light blue and track another person selecting darker blue.
Reported competing placements prompt an invitation into the thread and a promise to contact the named placers individually.
Participants judge themselves unable to defend against anticipated retaliation if expansion takes the neighbour's pixels.
Keeping the outer border black spares the work above and avoids provoking its makers.
Neighbour restraint here rests on anticipated defensive disadvantage without a documented bilateral settlement.
Judging newly taken neighbour pixels indefensible supplies the stated reason for sparing that work while retaining the existing mark.
A proposed site left of an existing logo answers a helper's offer to join without claiming that an earlier work was lost.
Participants assess unused room for expansion and favour current spacing because the adjacent construction is uncertain.
Members credit a maker, praise the logo, exclaim at its image, and congratulate the group through the final report.
The final reply records closure and reports a permanent mark intact except for two border pixels.
Acclaim of existing work opens another expansion, while a later post explicitly makes completed expansion the basis for further growth.
Design preferences can continue after placement ends, so proposals require separate evidence of enactment before explaining changed pixels.
The starter follows the collaboration call with a progress report at the same coordinates and another request for help.
Starting and calling coincide in the initial proposal, with the tiny-logo report renewing the request rather than establishing a separate starting stage.
An explicit join answers the collaboration call, supporting the response sequence without establishing silent placing or the general preference mechanism.
Celebration can mark a provisional achievement that immediately invites further expansion rather than a settled final design.
Celebration and fate reporting can coincide in one turn without showing that marking caused a separate preservation activity.
Open critique and internal agreement show drawing choices without establishing formal organising arrangements elsewhere or testing a cross-room frequency claim.
Competing colours and promised contact do not establish repair motives, keepers' knowledge, completed notification, or design loss caused by failed communication.
The room's internal border agreement does not document reciprocal terms or negotiations with the neighbour.
Avoiding neighbour provocation and inviting colour discussion leave attacks on other works unobserved rather than disproved.
A proposed small site beside an existing logo does not establish an earlier loss or relocation after erasure.
Reporting a frozen mark as permanent records its fate without documenting reuse, another canvas, or a continuing collective.
Named recolourers and promised messages establish neither automation nor exclusively manual placement.
Related logos serve as landmarks without documenting exchanged help or reciprocal obligations.
Proximity to related logos does not establish coalition membership or joint defence.
Anticipating retaliation and declining colour fighting do not establish an enacted contest with a rival carried on in talk.
Respecting the work above and choosing a spot beside another logo do not demonstrate a host ruling over a guest mark.
Promised contact targets individual colour placers without establishing a representative carrying terms between rooms.
The collaboration post and deleted-body help title cannot establish host restrictions on canvas discussion.
The logo call and ambiguous surviving title provide no evidence of the host being keyed as an April Fools prank.
Related logos and an unnamed neighbour do not establish an inherited quarrel carried onto the canvas.
Brand colours and an unexplained exclamation do not establish inherited lore, ideological belonging, or allegiance to a colour faction.
Related communities are landmarks and the feared neighbour is unnamed, leaving an inherited tie naming an attacked rival unobserved.
Colour discussion and permission to object concern design without stating limits on who can commit the room to inter-room terms.
Reporting two imperfect border pixels does not document cleanup, correction of an event claim, or contest over the version kept.
A promise to message individual recolourers and an external design link do not establish moving the room's planning into a chat.
Discovering the event and asking where its logo is do not establish questions or explanations about rules, controls, or picture meanings.
Joining after discovering the event does not state that the mark brought a newcomer or returning member into the room.
An isolated exclamation at the image does not establish a new canvas joke or its uptake.
A call to build and a declaration of community effort do not establish a new canvas room forming around the mark.
The invitation to discuss competing colours documents no dispute over offensive words, slurs, or hate symbols.
Crediting a maker does not establish seeking attention from staff, companies, or the press outside the canvas effort.
The practical retaliation rationale does not establish an argument over whether covering another work is fair.
Inviting colour discussion does not document personal abuse, stress-induced withdrawal, apology, or repaired member relations.
Promised messages to recolourers do not establish hiding plans, monitoring rivals, or infiltrating another venue.
Competing recolouring does not establish opposition to canvas posts motivating sabotage of the room's mark.
Maintenance intentions and a final accomplishment report supply no evidence of personal time, device, or cost constraints.
Failure to see a logo at given coordinates does not identify a site fault or a technical workaround.
Naming neighbouring logos does not establish dual membership or members being torn between rooms.
Completed letters, preventive border restraint, and proposed maintenance do not establish a distinct transition into actual repair labour.
The preventive border choice documents neither repair pressure nor talks with the neighbour.
Restraint has an explicit retaliation rationale, but no reciprocal settlement establishes the proposed antecedent.
Identified recolourers and maintenance intentions do not document upkeep strain leading to scripts or spare accounts.
The final fate report contains no decision to carry the temporary effort into another purpose or venue.
Predicted inability to defend newly taken neighbour pixels does not establish failure to hold the existing spot followed by relocation.
Coordinates and externally linked modular designs do not reveal an agreed pixel template settling the continuing design discussion.
Requests for readers' help do not establish maintenance strain causing assistance to be sought or received from other rooms.
The internal border choice documents neither reciprocal terms nor a subsequent exchange of help.
Calls to build are documented, but avoiding neighbour provocation supplies no attack call testing the proposed progression.
Restraint responds to an anticipated threat rather than a documented attack call, leaving the refusal mechanism untested.
The internal border agreement records no attack call answered through a truce or deal with another room.
Concern about possible retaliation does not establish an attack producing rivalry talk.
Neighbour proximity and proposed maintenance do not establish a sequence from defensive strain to coalition membership.
Visible calls lack evidence of a canvas-post flood or consequent host intervention.
Internal design agreement and discussion invitations establish neither inter-room terms nor a subsequent refusal or statement of representational limits.
